newsitem.title: USA: Sterling Chemicals acquires Cytec unit.
newsitem.headline: Sterling Chemicals acquires Cytec unit.

text.p: Sterling Chemicals Holdings Inc said on Monday that it has acquired the acrylic fibers business of Cytec Industries Inc for $100 million.
Also, Sterling assumed $9 million in liabilities and contingent liabilities, mostly for retiree health care and environmental reserves, Sterling said.
Sterling said the company anticipates minimal cash outlay for these liabilities and contingent liabilities over the next five years.

Sterling Chemicals said the acquisition of the acrylic fibers business was financed with approximately $80 million of new debt borrowed from existing bank and other senior lenders and approximately $10 million from the sale of additional common stock to employees and existing shareholders, Sterling Chemicals said. In addition, approximately $10 million of 10 percent "pay in kind" preferred stock was issued to Cytec Industries. The preferred stock is redeemable at par by the company at any time and at the election of Cytec Industries after 12-1/2 years, Sterling Chemicals said.
The acrylic fibers manufacturing facility is located near Pensacola, Fla., the company said.
The fibers business, which has expected 1996 revenues of $140 million, has approximately 300 employees, all of whom will be retained after the transaction closes, Sterling Chemicals said.
